RetailAgent / Video

When an agent chooses the wrong moment.

RetailAgent: Structured Adverse Timing in Self-Conditioned Multimodal LLM Trading Agents

Yupeng Zhang, Liuyuan Jiang, Hongyi Huang, Bingheng Li, Lisha Chen

Project pageRead the paper

Ready to recordNarration and storyboard draft

~2 minutesFive scenes with diagram pauses

Recorded video will be added here when available.

0:00–0:20

Two agents can hold a stock equally often and earn different returns because they choose different intervals. RetailAgent studies that timing component.

On screen: Show two schedules with the same number of long decisions on a single return path.

0:20–0:45

The LLM sees an anonymized intraday history, chooses long or flat, and then observes the next return. The experiment controls what information is available at decision time.

On screen: Show history, action, and then the subsequent return in sequence.

0:45–1:10

The timing metric removes average exposure on each stock-day. It measures whether the agent selects comparatively favorable intervals on the same price path.

On screen: Subtract the mean action from each decision and display the timing sum.

1:10–1:35

The principal text condition reports negative timing of 45.7 basis points in magnitude. Shuffling the saved schedule attenuates the effect. The paper also tests how self-authored memory changes persistence.

On screen: Compare intact text timing with the two shuffle-control values from Table 1.

1:35–2:00

The action traces reveal sequential structure in the evaluated policies. Measuring timing alongside exposure shows how self-authored memory changes the agent’s decisions.

On screen: Show controlled audit, then transaction costs and market feedback as open study directions.
